did_you_know.text: Did you know? Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. This chapter focuses on organizing the priestly families for service in the Temple.
Did you know? Nadab and Abihu died before Aaron and had no sons, so the priesthood continued through Eleazar and Ithamar.
Did you know? King David organized the divisions of the priests together with Zadok, a descendant of Eleazar, and Ahimelech, a descendant of Ithamar.
Did you know? Because there were more male heads of families among Eleazar’s descendants than among Ithamar’s, sixteen divisions were assigned to Eleazar’s descendants and eight to Ithamar’s.
Did you know? The divisions were assigned by lot to establish an orderly, fair, and mutually accepted arrangement between the descendants of Eleazar and Ithamar.
Did you know? Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a Levite scribe, recorded the order of the divisions in the presence of the king, the officials, the priests, and the heads of the families.
Did you know? The first division chosen by lot was Jehoiarib, followed by Jedaiah; this began the listing of the twenty-four priestly divisions.
Did you know? The twenty-fourth division chosen by lot was Maaziah. The entire list was intended to establish the order of the priests’ service in the house of the Lord.
Did you know? After listing the priestly divisions, the chapter goes on to list other Levite families, including the descendants of Amram, Rehabiah, the Izharites, Micah, and Ishiah.

Did you know? The Levites also cast lots in the presence of David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the families, just as the descendants of Aaron had done, to organize their service according to their ancestral families.
